question: According to an analysis by C4ADS1, between January 2025 and July 2026, the Russian ‘air shadow fleet’ carried out at least 75 flights transporting personnel and military equipment for the Africa Corps in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger. Some of the operators involved have not yet been sanctioned by the EU.

At the same time, the EU is channelling significant funds to these countries – between 2021 and 2024, this amounted to EUR 151 million for Mali, EUR 283 million for Burkina Faso and EUR 382.34 million for Niger, even though certain forms of cooperation have been suspended. 1.

Is the Commission investigating and preparing targeted restrictive measures against airlines, aircraft, their owners and operators involved in the transport of personnel or military equipment for Russia’s Africa Corps?

Is the Commission investigating whether countries in receipt of EU funds are allowing their territory, airports or other infrastructure to be used to provide logistical support for Russia’s Africa Corps or to circumvent EU sanctions?

Does the Commission consider it acceptable for the EU to continue providing significant financial support to countries which also allow Russia to use their territory or infrastructure to support Russian military operations, and is it prepared to suspend this support or make it conditional on demonstrable cooperation by these countries in preventing the activities of the Russian ‘air shadow fleet’ and the circumvention of EU sanctions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (11.11.2026) In the context of Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine, Flight Unit 224, responsible for the greatest number of flights from Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger according to the C4ADS report, is subject to EU restrictive measures. The EU has also designated the airline’s General Director.

It has prohibited the sale, supply, transfer or export to Russia, or for use in Russia, of goods used in the aviation field, as well as insurance and re-insurance of such goods. The EU has also adopted export restrictions on relevant jet fuel and fuel additives.

It imposed an airspace and airport ban on Russian air carriers, Russian-registered aircraft, aircraft owned, chartered or controlled by Russian persons or entities, and other aircraft used for non-scheduled flights where a Russian person or entity can effectively determine the place or time of take-off or landing.

Furthermore, the Wagner Group (also known as Africa Corps), as well as several linked individuals and entities, are listed for serious human rights abuses, inter alia, in the Central African Republic, Sudan and Mali.

The Commission has reviewed EU-funded programmes in the countries concerned, and cooperation with Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger has been adapted to the new geopolitical context: no funds are channelled through the authorities, and the actions implemented are for the direct benefit of the population. The EU will continue to assess the situation with Member States and adapt its cooperation as appropriate.
